In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of signal parameter tracking and estimation in a low SNR regime with 1-bit ADCs at the receiver.
the analysis and design of signal parameter estimation algorithms for low-resolution measurement data.
the analysis of the achievable tracking error in the case of a simplistic receiver that is based on a low resolution ADC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for the case of slow parameter evolution, a low resolution ADC at the receiver can be a viable alternative to a high resolution one.

for a given SNR and a given channel evolution rate, there exists a quantization resolution which is the best trade-off between the cost of a higher ADC resolution and the achievable estimation performance.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, the loss in performance for 1-bit ADCs can be significantly reduced if the channel parameters are tracked over time.

, if the temporal evolution of channel parameters is known or can be reliably estimated from the measurement data, the performance loss due 1-bit ADC is significantly smaller than the loss for the case of stationary channels.
the performance loss for channel parameter estimation with 1-bit ADC is significantly less than the 1.96 dB loss for the ideal case of low SNR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance loss in dB of a 1-bit receiver is not necessarily 3 dB for medium to high SNR.
a 1-bit ADC at the receiver is not necessarily a severe limitation in terms of the achievable estimation accuracy.
the performance loss in dB of a simplistic receiver can be significantly smaller than indicated by classical analysis, if the channel parameters evolve slowly in time.
